title: The Mending of the State
summary: The calm before the storm. A young sultan, tributary to Castile and deep in debt, sets the state in order: the Catalan privileges, the war on Aragon and the peace of Balansiyya, the two ṭāʾifas of the east, Morocco's defeat of 1340, the Jamāʿa of 1344 and the crown it strengthened, and the debt paid down. It ends the day Morocco declares war again.

title: The Balance
summary: Granada on the scales between the three crowns of Iberia and the Marīnids, from the season sovereignty first slipped below 50. The war of 1346 brought five great victories, the Peace of Qurṭuba (January 1349) and the quiet bargain for Qarmūna and the silver of Qusanṭīna (May 1351); Morocco's surrender in June 1351 ended its alliance with Granada and its foothold on this shore. The book stays open until the Strait turns firmly in Granada's favour. Written as it happens.

title: The Pestilence
summary: The Black Death, from the first rumours out of the east in 1346 and the hospitals the amir raised against it in Gharnāṭa, Mālaqa and al-Mariyya, to the day it left the last town of the realm, 27 January 1352, the Day of ʿArafa on which the amir stood on the plain. Its heart is the reshaping of Granada itself: the most urban realm in Iberia, two in five of its people living in cities where Castile had one in twenty, lost 42% of its people in four years, the cities and their burghers and scholars worst of all, hospitals or no. Ran beside the Book of the Balance.

title: The Call
summary: Education and the return of Islam to al-Andalus as the Emirate grows: roads through the mountains, libraries in the cities of the south and then the north, and the slow reconversion of Qurṭuba and the valley of the great river, purged of Islam and of Andalusī culture during the Castilian occupation. Written as it happens.
